questions.q: Define irony and symbolism in your own words, giving one example from daily life for each (not from the poems).
questions.a: Irony: A situation where the outcome is contrary to what was expected (e.g., a fire station burning down). Symbolism: Using an object to represent a deeper idea (e.g., a dove representing peace). A wrong answer that defines irony as "sarcasm" or "lying" reveals confusion between verbal irony and situational irony; a wrong answer that equates symbolism with "metaphor" shows inability to distinguish a sustained representative object from a direct comparison.

questions.q: In "नहीं वोस्यक", the poet repeatedly says "यह फूल नहीं वोस्यक" (this flower is not a night-flower). Explain why this repetition creates irony rather than mere negation.
questions.a: The repetition sets up an expectation of a night-flower (associated with darkness, passivity, fleeting beauty) only to replace it with a flower of "श्रम" (labor), "वसंत" (spring), and "उन्मुक्तता" (freedom). The irony lies in the contrast between the stereotypical romantic image of a night-flower and the robust, labor-born reality the poet champions. A student who says "it just emphasizes it's not a night flower" misses the thematic contrast and treats irony as simple denial.

questions.q: Identify one symbol in "मैंने देखा, एक चाँद" and explain how the poet develops its symbolic meaning across the poem. Quote the relevant lines by description (not full stanza).
questions.a: The moon (चाँद) functions as a symbol of fragile freedom. Initially described as a "white flower" (सफेद फूल), its color fades at the touch of a gentle breeze (मंद पवन का स्पर्श), and the moonlight spreads like "olive oil" (जैतून के तेल) carrying the "scent of freedom" (उन्मुक्तता की गंध). The progression from static beauty → vulnerability → expansive fragrance maps the journey of freedom from ideal to threatened to pervasive. A wrong answer that only identifies "moon = beauty" ignores the dynamic development and the specific abstract idea (freedom) tied to the symbol.

questions.q: Compare the use of irony in the two poems. How does the target of irony differ in "नहीं वोस्यक" versus "मैंने देखा, एक चाँद"?
questions.a: In "नहीं वोस्यक", irony targets societal categorization: the label "वोस्यक" (night-flower) represents passive, decorative beauty imposed by tradition, which the poet rejects in favor of labor-born vitality. In "मैंने देखा, एक चाँद", irony is subtler — the moon, a celestial symbol of constancy, is shown as fragile and changeable (color fading at a breeze's touch), ironically mirroring how freedom appears eternal but is actually vulnerable. A student who claims both poems use irony to "criticize society" without distinguishing the specific targets (labels vs. illusions of permanence) shows superficial comparative analysis.

questions.q: Evaluate the effectiveness of the symbol "श्रम" (labor) in "नहीं वोस्यक". Does treating labor as a cultivator of the flower strengthen or weaken the poem's message? Justify.
questions.a: It strengthens the message because it transforms labor from a burden into a creative, life-giving force — the flower *is* "वह फूल जिसे श्रम ने उगाया है" (the flower that labor has grown). This personification makes the abstract dignity of labor tangible and beautiful, aligning with the poem's theme of redefining worth. A student who says "it's just a metaphor" fails to evaluate the symbolic weight: the symbol operates across the whole poem, not as a one-off comparison, and its effectiveness lies in making the political (labor rights) aesthetic.

questions.q: Write a 4-line stanza in Hindi that uses irony to describe a common school experience, and include one symbol that represents an abstract idea (e.g., hope, pressure, freedom). Do not copy from the textbook.
questions.a: Example: "घंटी बजी, कक्षा खाली / गुरुजी बोले, 'पढ़ो मतवाली' / दीवार पर टँगा एक टूटा पंखा / घूमता रहा, थकान का गवाह।" Irony: teacher tells students not to study (opposite of expectation). Symbol: broken fan = relentless exhaustion. A poor answer that writes a sincere description without contradiction (no irony) or uses a direct comparison like "पढ़ाई पहाड़ है" (simile, not symbol) shows inability to generate the devices independently.
